jobs.title: Technical Delivery Manager
jobs.jd_full:
Company Description

Are you ready to join the forefront of technology innovation with Netcompany?  

As one of the fastest growing technology companies, we are disrupting the marketplace and revolutionizing the way businesses operate. Our vision is to be the leading digital challenger in Europe whilst evolving the next generation of IT consulting.

Operating across both public and private sectors, we offer a comprehensive range of services from application development and seamless cloud migration to program delivery and service operations, our offerings are designed to meet diverse business needs.

Job Description

Netcompany is looking for a Technical Delivery Manager to drive forward our delivery capability and deliver the optimum solutions to the clients. As a Delivery Manager, in our Application Development unit, you will be working on a variety of projects. Based in London or Leeds, this is a great opportunity to join one of the most exciting, innovative, prestigious and forward-thinking technology-enabled organisations in the UK. 
 

Key responsibilities:

  • Lead the end-to-end delivery of complex digital services, ensuring agreed outcomes are achieved within scope, budget, timescales and quality expectations.
  • Provide hands-on agile delivery leadership across one or more multidisciplinary teams, adapting ways of working to the delivery context and undertaking Scrum Master responsibilities where appropriate, including facilitating planning, daily stand-ups, reviews, retrospectives and backlog refinement.
  • Create the conditions for effective agile delivery by removing blockers, managing dependencies and helping teams continuously improve how they work.
  • Work closely with Product Managers to translate product strategy and priorities into achievable delivery plans, balancing user needs, business objectives and technical constraints.
  • Lead multidisciplinary teams comprising delivery, product, engineering, architecture, quality assurance, business analysis, data and user-centred design professionals, building team capability and supporting individuals to grow and perform effectively.
  • Ensure user-centred design disciplines, including user research, service design, interaction design and content design, are integrated throughout delivery.
  • Support services through the GDS delivery lifecycle, from Discovery and Alpha through Beta and Live, ensuring alignment with the Government Service Standard and Technology Code of Practice.
  • Plan and coordinate GDS service assessments, including assessment readiness, evidence gathering, team preparation and the management of recommendations arising from assessments.
  • Maintain effective delivery controls, including delivery plans, RAID logs, dependency management, resource forecasting, governance reporting and stakeholder communications.
  • Take a hands-on approach to Jira and Confluence, ensuring backlogs, workflows, dashboards, documentation, decisions and delivery reporting are accurate and actively maintained.
  • Manage delivery across complex technology environments involving system integration, legacy platforms, cloud services and third-party suppliers.
  • Provide clear and transparent reporting on delivery progress, risks, dependencies, finances and outcomes to senior management, clients and governance forums.
  • Build trusted relationships with clients, stakeholders, suppliers and team members, constructively challenging decisions where required to protect delivery outcomes.
  • Contribute to the wider delivery management community through knowledge sharing, coaching and mentoring less experienced colleagues.

Qualifications

  • Extensive experience of leading complex digital or technology delivery within government or the wider public sector.
  • Strong practical knowledge of agile delivery methods, alongside experience of traditional and hybrid delivery approaches, with the ability to select and adapt the most appropriate with experience performing both Delivery Manager and Scrum Master responsibilities.
  • Previous experience in a software development or engineering role, with a strong understanding of the software development lifecycle, technical architectures, coding practices and development methodologies.
  • Demonstrable experience of leading multidisciplinary digital teams that include Product Management, engineering, quality assurance, business analysis and user-centred design professionals.
  • Strong understanding of the respective accountabilities of Delivery Managers and Product Managers, with evidence of effective collaboration to manage priorities, roadmaps and delivery outcomes.
  • Advanced, hands-on experience of Jira and Confluence or other project management tools including backlog management, workflows, dashboards, reporting and delivery documentation.
  • Strong knowledge of the software delivery lifecycle, including Discovery, Alpha, Beta, Live and ongoing service improvement.
  • Experience of delivery planning, dependency management, risk and issue management, resource forecasting and governance reporting.
  • Experience of managing system integration initiatives involving multiple technologies, delivery teams and third-party suppliers.
  • Proven ability to remove delivery blockers, manage competing priorities and create an environment in which teams can deliver effectively.
  • Excellent facilitation, coaching and servant-leadership skills, with the ability to embed agile behaviours and drive continuous improvement.
  • Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, including the ability to build trust, communicate complex delivery matters clearly and constructively challenge senior stakeholders.
  • Experience of contributing to a professional community through knowledge sharing, coaching and mentoring.
  • A recognised agile delivery or Scrum Master qualification, or equivalent demonstrable professional experience.
  • Willingness to work within a hybrid model and travel occasionally to client or delivery locations.

Additional Information

Benefits include

  • Hybrid working model with some flexible working
  • 25 days’ holiday
  • Private Medical Health care via Vitality
  • Pension contribution, Life Assurance
  • Professional certifications supported as part of learning and development.
  • A range of retail discounts to enhance your lifestyle, encompassing restaurants, supermarkets, travel, leisure activities and health and well-being services.
  • Access to our Employee Resource Groups, our groups represent diverse backgrounds and provide a platform for colleagues to connect, learn, and support one another.

Company information

At Netcompany, we pride ourselves on our entrepreneurial spirit and our capacity for doing things differently. Our culture is built on fostering low bureaucracy, emphasizing high agility and promoting flexibility, enabling everyone to contribute their best.

Our journey began in the UK with the acquisition of Hunter Macdonald in 2017. As one of Northern Europe’s most accomplished IT companies, we have expanded our headcount globally to 7400+ employees and have offices in UK, Denmark, Norway, Poland, Holland and Vietnam.

Netcompany is committed to providing an inclusive and barrier-free recruitment process for anyone wishing to apply for a job with us.  We operate a Disability Confident Interview Scheme which means that we offer guaranteed interviews to all applicants with a disability who meet the minimum criteria for a role. Applicants are asked to opt in, so please let us know if you wish your application to be considered under this scheme.

If you need any reasonable adjustments or extra support during the recruitment process, please contact us at [email protected].

jobs.title: Product Manager - AI Augmented
jobs.jd_full:
Human Interest is on a mission to ensure that people in all lines of work have access to retirement benefits. 

More than half of all working Americans are not saving enough for their future. Too often, it’s because they are employed by a company that doesn’t offer a retirement plan. Human Interest is changing that by making it affordable and accessible for small and medium-sized businesses to offer employees a path to financial independence through retirement savings.

We’re a high-growth fintech company changing the retirement industry. We are backed by a number of investors. This includes funding from Marshall Wace and Baillie Gifford, as well as top investors such as BlackRock, TPG (The Rise Fund), SoftBank, Glynn Capital, NewView Capital, USVP, Wing, Uncork, and more.

About the role

Product management is changing. The best product managers no longer just write requirements and wait for engineering; they prototype their own ideas, pressure-test them with data, and use AI to move from problem to validated solution in days rather than quarters. We are looking for product managers who have embraced that shift and who want to apply it to one of the biggest unsolved problems in America: helping working people save for retirement.

You will independently own whole projects, each made up of multiple features, within a product area. You will turn the broader product vision into concrete plans your engineering team can deliver, and partner closely with Engineering, Design, Operations, Customer Success, and Compliance to ship accurate, reliable work that achieves the results it was meant to. You will do this as an AI-augmented builder: using modern AI tooling both to sharpen how you work and to help shape products that increasingly work on our customers’ behalf.

What you get to do every day

  • Own multi-feature projects end to end, from discovery through launch and iteration. Translate the broader vision for your product area into concrete feature plans, and give your team a clear picture of the customer experience you’re building.
  • Prioritize work based on expected customer and business impact. Define clear success metrics aligned with long-term goals, and report on outcomes, not just completion of tasks.
  • Notice when something you shipped isn’t achieving the desired results, dig into why, and recommend changes.
  • Produce clear requirements and artifacts that unblock engineering to deliver high-quality work on time, with accuracy and auditability built in.
  • Ensure your projects meet compliance standards, and create processes to validate data accuracy within your product area.
  • Develop deep knowledge of customer problems in your area. Combine qualitative feedback and quantitative data to represent user needs and anticipate requirements beyond what customers explicitly ask for.
  • Communicate effectively with engineering, design, and partner teams, manage tradeoffs and timelines within your projects, and explain complex concepts in simple, accessible terms.

How you work with AI

We expect our product managers to use AI to work smarter and solve problems faster, and to bring good judgment about where AI belongs in the product itself.

  • Prototype rapidly. Use tools such as Figma Make, Claude Code, Codex, or similar to explore, validate, and demonstrate ideas yourself, so you can align your team on direction with a working artifact rather than a document.
  • Compress the busywork. Apply AI to speed up research synthesis, requirements drafting, data exploration, and analysis so you spend your time on judgment, customer understanding, and getting the details right.
  • Build AI into the product. Spot where copilots, agents, and intelligent automation could genuinely improve the customer experience within your projects, and work with engineering to define how they should behave across success, failure, and edge cases.

What you bring to the role

  • Experience: 2+ years of product management experience, including independently delivering multi-feature projects with an engineering team in a technical product area. Experience with financial or other regulated products is a plus.
  • AI fluency: Hands-on use of AI tools to build and transform how you work, not just as a chatbot. You are comfortable vibe-coding front-end and UX changes yourself, and you can point to prototypes or interfaces where AI meaningfully changed the outcome or the pace.
  • Ownership mindset: High agency and high urgency. You own projects end to end, sweat the details, and stay with your work after launch to make sure it delivers.
  • Technical partnership: You have worked closely with engineers on technical products, can dig into issues to understand their root cause, and ask the questions that get to a good fix.
  • Analytical rigor: You are data-driven, use data to make decisions and measure results, and care equally about accuracy and timeliness.
  • Business curiosity: You want to understand how the business works and how your projects move the metrics that matter.
  • Communication: Clear, detail-oriented written and verbal communication, with the ability to explain technical concepts to engineers and non-technical partners alike.
  • Education: Degree in Computer Science, Business, or a related field.

Why you will love working at Human Interest

Human Interest is tackling one of our country’s biggest challenges - closing the retirement gap. You’ll be instrumental in architecting and scaling solutions that bring financial security to employees at small and medium-sized businesses nationwide. We’ve made significant progress, but there is still growth ahead, offering you a unique opportunity to solve complex problems, drive innovation, and advance your career alongside a dedicated, mission-driven team. We value hard work and recognize that our team’s contributions are key to our continued success.

Join Human Interest and make a lasting impact by shaping the future of retirement.

Our operating principles define how we work together as a team. They reflect Human Interest’s unique view on what’s important and what’s right. Documenting this core aspect of our culture helps employees make good decisions on their own. It also helps candidates considering career opportunities critically evaluate whether they will thrive at Human Interest. 

  • Customer obsession: We’re all about creating amazing experiences for our customers. We put their needs first and go the extra mile to make them smile.
  • Long-Term Orientation: We’re not just playing for today; we’re building a legacy. We think big, plan strategically, and invest in our future.
  • Autonomous and Accountable Teams: We trust our team members to take ownership and make smart decisions. We empower you to be your best self!
  • An Escalating Bar for Talent and Performance: We’re constantly raising the bar and challenging ourselves to be better. We believe in growth and continuous improvement.
  • Fundamental Optimism: We see the glass as half full (and then we fill it up with more amazing ideas!). We believe in the power of positivity and the potential for greatness.

Compensation - At Human Interest, there are a number of factors that are used to determine the appropriate pay range for each position. We take into account the cost of labor for each position in various markets across the U.S. The base salary for this position spans $135,000 - $180,000 and represents the minimum in our lowest geographic region to a maximum in our highest geographic region. The salary we offer to a new employee within this range is based on their location within the U.S., their relevant job-related skills, and experience. At Human Interest, base salary is one component of the overall total rewards package. Depending on the position, additional compensation components such as bonuses, commissions, and equity may be offered. All of our employees are offered a robust suite of physical, financial, and mental wellness benefits. In compliance with applicable laws, we do not inquire about salary history, or about criminal history prior to a conditional offer of employment.

Benefits - 

  • A great 401(k) plan: Our own! Our 401(k) includes a dollar-for-dollar employer match up to 4% of compensation (immediately vested) and $0 plan fees
  • Top-of-the-line health plans, as well as dental and vision insurance
  • Competitive time off and parental leave
  • Addition Wealth:  Unlimited access to digital tools, financial professionals, and a knowledge center to help you understand your equity and support your financial wellness
  • Lyra: Enhanced Mental Health Support for Employees and dependents
  • Carrot: Fertility healthcare and family forming benefits
  • Candidly:  Student loan resource to help you and your family plan, borrow, and repay student debt
  • Monthly work-from-home stipend; quarterly lifestyle stipend
  • Engaging team-building experiences, ranging from virtual social events to team offsites, promoting collaboration and camaraderie.

We’re a great place to work (but don’t take our word for it) 

Here’s a list of our awards and accolades:

  • Certified as a Great Place To Work® (2023-2025)
  • Fortune Best Place to Work in the Bay Area (2024)
  • Best Places to Work by Built In (2023-2024)
  • America’s Best Startup Employers by Forbes (2020-2022, 2024)
  • A Top Company by Y Combinator (2020-2023)
  • Inc. Fastest Growing Companies (2021)

Human Interest is an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, veteran or military status, pregnancy, or any other characteristics protected under federal, state, or local laws. Employment with Human Interest is at-will, meaning either you or the company may terminate employment at any time, with or without cause or notice, except as otherwise provided by law or written agreement.

We are committed to making every stage of our application process fully accessible to all individuals. If you need a reasonable accommodation at any point in the process, please let us know at applicantaccommodations@humaninterest.com.

Protect yourself against fraud and identity theft. Apply to our open positions directly via our careers page on Greenhouse. Human Interest will never ask applicants for their financial or banking information as part of our application process. All legitimate communication will come from a @humaninterest.com email address. If you have questions, please reach out to us directly at careers@humaninterest.com

Please note Human Interest does not accept unsolicited resumes from any source other than directly from candidates. We will not consider resumes from vendors, including and without limitation search firms, staffing agencies, fee-based referral services, and recruiting agencies. 

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider employment-qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. We comply with CCPA guidelines.

jobs.title: Lead Product Manager, New Customer Experience
jobs.jd_full:
About LawnStarter

LawnStarter is the nation’s leading on-demand marketplace for lawn care and outdoor services, with over $750M in bookings. We’re expanding beyond lawn care to become the one-stop shop for home services: three brands (LawnStarter, Lawn Love, Home Gnome), one shared platform.

About Product at LawnStarter

Our BHAG: 1+ job per household, every year. Getting there means winning on four fronts at once: more customers, more Pros, excellent service for both sides, and an AI-run company that moves faster than its size should allow.

About the First Service Experience at LawnStarter

Every new customer meets us the same way. They land on our home page or marketing site, then move through a signup and booking flow where they get a quote, pick a service and a schedule, and pay. That flow runs across all three brands and brings in most of the company’s new customers.

We built it many years ago. It’s too long, and we lose customers at too many steps. So the real question isn’t how to remove a step. It’s whether the experience designed still makes sense at all, or whether it should be rethought entirely as an AI-native, agentic experience.

The Role

You’ll own the consumer’s first service experience: everything from the moment someone first encounters LawnStarter through signing up and booking their first service. You’ll decide what that experience should become, then build it with engineering, design, operations, marketing, and data.

This is not a funnel-optimization job. We want someone who looks at a five-year-old flow, asks what a homeowner would want if we started from nothing today, and then ships the answer.

As Lead PM, you’re an individual contributor with Lead-level scope and no direct reports. You’ll work closely with the Consumer Experience lead, the Pro Experience PM, the Pricing PM, and the Conversational AI & Agents lead. You’ll report to the Sr. Director of Product.

What makes this role different:

  • A rebuild, not a tune-up. You’re rethinking the experience from first principles, not polishing the one we have.
  • AI-native from the first screen. You’ll decide whether a form is even the right way to sign up anymore.
  • Every new customer passes through your work. Across three brands, this is how people meet LawnStarter.

What You’ll Own

  • The vision: What the first service experience should become, and the plan to get there.
  • The home page and marketing site: The first impression, and the first decision a customer makes about us.
  • Signup and booking for all three brands: LawnStarter, Lawn Love, and Home Gnome.
  • Funnel data: The numbers that show where customers move forward and where they leave.
  • Quotes, services, and scheduling: How a customer gets a price, picks a service, and chooses when it happens.
  • Payment: Checkout, including Apple Pay and Google Pay.

Problems to Solve

Deciding whether today’s experience should exist at all.
You’ll start from what a homeowner needs to book their first service and work backward. Every step we have today has to earn its place again, and you’ll defend each call with evidence.

Designing an AI-native, agentic way to sign up.
Someone who wants their lawn mowed shouldn’t have to learn our product to book it. What can an agent handle for them, and where does a person still want control? You’ll answer with prototypes in front of real customers, not opinions in a meeting.

Rebuilding without breaking what works.
This flow brings in most of our new customers. You’ll need a path that proves the new experience works with real customers before it replaces the old one. Bold and careful at once: that’s the job.

Moving levers you don’t own.
Signup touches pricing, Pro supply, and operations. Change how customers book and you change what Pros see and how jobs get priced. You’ll work through the people who own those levers and bring them along on a vision that changes their world too.

What Success Looks Like (Year 1)

  • A vision leadership rallies behind: A clear picture of the reimagined first service experience, grounded in what customers need.
  • A first piece of it, live: A meaningful part of that experience shipped to real customers. Not a deck.
  • Signup conversion goes up: More of the people who find us become customers.
  • More customers sign up for their first service: The reimagined experience gets more households to that first booking.
  • First service CSAT is high: Customers rate their first service experience highly (customer satisfaction, CSAT).

Who You Are:

Experience: Customer obsessed with 6+ years in consumer product management, focused on consumer experience.

A visionary who ships. You look at an experience everyone has accepted and ask why it exists. Then you build the replacement. Is your instinct to improve what’s there, one step at a time? Then this isn’t your role.

Customer-obsessed, for the long run. You care whether a customer converts and whether they’re glad they did. Short-term signups never win over the customer’s experience in your book. Someone who’d juice conversion at the customer’s expense won’t last here.

An AI builder. You’ve shipped AI-powered or agentic consumer experiences. You prototype new signup experiences with LLMs and agents, read customer transcripts to hear where people get stuck, and use AI to pull apart funnel data in an afternoon. If you’ve only watched AI from the sidelines, this role is unlikely to be a good fit.

Your own analyst. You run your own funnel analysis and product analytics, and you know which step loses people before anyone builds you a dashboard. If you need someone else to pull your numbers, this is unlikely to be a good fit.

A strategist and a design partner. You set priorities, say no with reasons, and work beside design from the first sketch. PMs who hand designers a finished spec, or wait to be handed finished designs, will struggle.

A plus: marketplace and personalization experience. You know a change to signup ripples into Pros, pricing, and operations, and you’ve built experiences that adapt to each customer. Treat signup as a self-contained form and you’ll miss half the problem.

Minimum Bachelor’s degree in business, analytics, engineering, design, or a related field, plus 6+ years of product management experience on consumer-facing products.

This Role Is NOT

  • A people-management role. You’re an individual contributor with no direct reports.

  • A growth-tactics role. If your best work is button tests and drip-email tweaks, this isn’t the fit. We need the experience reimagined, not tuned.

  • For someone without a real consumer experience background. If you haven’t spent your career building for consumers, please don’t apply.

  • A strategy-only seat. You’ll prototype with AI tools, read transcripts, and get into the data yourself. If you’d rather only set direction, this will frustrate you.

  • A role with a big team, a clean stack, or every lever. We’re frugal: a lean engineering team and a partly legacy stack, and much of this experience touches levers other teams own. You’ll get impact by choosing carefully, using AI to outpace headcount, and influencing what you don’t control.

  • Equity: Every new customer meets LawnStarter through the experience you build. Equity means you share in the company value that creates.

  • Base salary: $170,000 to $210,000

  • Healthcare: Medical, dental, and vision

  • Location: Fully remote (US). Rethinking an experience from first principles takes long stretches of focus, and remote work protects them.

  • PTO: Flexible. We focus on results. Take what you need.

LawnStarter provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, or genetics. We comply with applicable state and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment.

jobs.title: Lead Product Manager, AI Agents
jobs.jd_full:
About LawnStarter

LawnStarter is the nation’s leading on-demand marketplace for lawn care and outdoor services, with over $750M in bookings. We’re expanding beyond lawn care to become the one-stop shop for home services: three brands (LawnStarter, Lawn Love, Home Gnome), one shared platform.

About Product at LawnStarter

Our BHAG: 1+ job per household, every year. Getting there means winning on four fronts at once: more customers, more Pros, excellent service for both sides, and an AI-run company that moves faster than its size should allow.

About AI Agents at LawnStarter

Our mission: power every AI experience. For homeowners and for Pros (the lawn care providers on our marketplace), conversational AI can do far more than answer questions. It can skip a service, reschedule a visit, or book a new one mid-conversation, even when the customer’s own AI agent is the one talking. And it doesn’t have to live only in a chat window: we’re bringing agentic experiences into the workflows homeowners and Pros already use, so the product does the work for them wherever they are. You’ll decide what that looks like for both sides, then ship it.

The Role

This is LawnStarter’s first core AI PM role. You’ll own our conversational AI and agent experiences for consumers and Pros: the chat, the actions it takes, the moment it hands off to a person, and how outside AI agents work with us. Beyond chat, you’ll bring agentic experiences into existing consumer and Pro workflows, so AI takes action inside the product rather than alongside it.

As Lead PM, you’re an individual contributor with Lead-level scope, reporting to the Sr. Director of Product. The AI experiences you power will often sit inside surfaces other PMs own, so you’ll share goals with the Customer Experience lead, the First Service Experience lead, and the Pro Experience PM, and build with engineering, applied science, design, data, customer service, and operations.

What makes this role different:

  • Fast, and at the center. Within a year, we expect AI to shape a meaningful share of how homeowners and Pros experience LawnStarter, and you’ll be at the center of making that happen. This role moves fast and rewards people who ship.
  • You’re the first. The evals, the guardrails, and the bar for “ready to ship” are yours to set.
  • The AI takes real actions. It reschedules and skips services on a live marketplace. No sandbox.
  • Two sides, one conversation. Everything you ship serves homeowners, Pros, or both, and an action for one changes the other’s day.

What You’ll Own

  • The AI roadmap: Where consumer AI and Pro AI go next, and the order we build it in.
  • Customer AI chat: Answering homeowners’ questions and completing tasks, like skipping or rescheduling a service.
  • AI chat in the Pros App: The AI experience Pros get inside the app they work from.
  • Agents inside existing workflows: AI that acts within the consumer and Pro flows people already use, not just in a chat window.
  • Customer-to-Pro messaging: How homeowners and Pros talk to each other.
  • The handoff to human support: When the bot passes a conversation to a support agent.
  • Outside AI agents: Letting a customer’s own agent, such as ChatGPT or Claude, work with us on their behalf.

Problems to Solve

From answering questions to solving problems.

A chatbot that explains how to reschedule is useful. One that understands what the customer or Pro actually needs, recommends the right thing, and then does it for them is a different product, and a riskier one. Sometimes the best answer isn’t the action they asked for: a skip might be better as a reschedule, or a one-time booking better as a plan. You’ll decide which actions the AI takes on its own, which need confirmation, and what happens when it gets one wrong.

Knowing when to hand off, and doing it well.
Some conversations belong with a person. Which ones? And can the bot tell before the customer gets frustrated? When the handoff comes, the support agent should pick up with full context so the customer doesn’t repeat themselves.

When the customer’s agent is the one asking.
Sometimes the one talking to LawnStarter won’t be a homeowner. It’ll be their own AI agent, such as ChatGPT, asking about a service, booking one, or changing it. You’ll work out what we let an outside agent do and how the customer stays in control.

Evals and guardrails for two audiences.
A good answer for a homeowner isn’t a good answer for a Pro. You’ll build the evals that tell us when an AI experience is good enough to ship and when its quality slips, plus the guardrails that keep it safe once it’s live.

What Success Looks Like (Year 1)

  • AI shaping the experience: AI experiences live for consumers and Pros, and shaping a meaningful share of how both sides interact with LawnStarter, measured by:

    • Share of conversations resolved by AI without a human (resolution or containment rate)
    • CSAT on AI conversations, for homeowners and Pros
    • Action accuracy: errors on reschedules, skips, and bookings stay below a set bar

  • Pros get more done because of AI: Pros spend less time on admin and coordination, and say AI makes them more productive.

  • More customers stay because AI makes service better: Consumer and Pro retention rises, driven by AI that resolves problems faster and improves the service experience.

Who You Are

Experience: 6+ years of product management, including at least 3 years launching AI products to customers (internal or external).

An AI builder who has shipped to real users. You’ve put AI products in front of real end users, whether in B2C, B2B, or B2B2C, and at least one was a chatbot or conversational AI running in production. You read transcripts to find where conversations break. If your AI work stopped at demos, prototypes, or a thin prompt wrapper that never met a real user, this isn’t your role.

The owner of quality. You write evals yourself. You know when an AI experience is good enough to ship, and when its quality starts to slip. Would you rather someone else define what “good” means? Then you’ll struggle here.

Fluent in agents and tool use. You understand what changes when an agent stops producing text and starts calling actions on real systems, and you design for the ways that goes wrong. PMs who treat AI as a feature bolted onto the side won’t last here.

A strategist who prioritizes with data. You set priorities, say no with reasons, and back each call with evidence. If your roadmaps run on instinct alone, this is unlikely to be a good fit.

A systems thinker. You see a product change as one part of a larger system and think through its second- and third-order effects before you ship. Here, that system is a marketplace: a change for customers almost always touches Pros, pricing, and operations too. You plan for those effects in the spec, not after launch. Marketplace experience helps, but what matters most is that you instinctively ask, “What else does this change?” If you’d rather ship your piece and let other teams deal with what it changes, this isn’t your role.

This Role Is NOT

  • A people-management role. You’re an individual contributor with no direct reports.
  • A research or ML-platform seat. If your AI career has been research or platform work that never reached end users, this isn’t the fit.
  • For AI skeptics. If you see AI as an add-on rather than the product, you’ll fight the job daily.
  • A strategy-only seat. You’ll write the evals and read the transcripts. Setting direction from a distance won’t work here.
  • A role with foundations already built. You’ll build the evals, the guardrails, and how we decide an AI experience is ready, not inherit them. We’re also lean and frugal, on a partly legacy stack.
  • Low-stakes. AI that reschedules or skips a service fails in front of customers and Pros, so the safety bar is high. And since your work lives inside surfaces other PMs own, you’ll lead through influence.

Bachelor’s degree in business, analytics, engineering, design, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience, plus 6+ years of product management experience on consumer-facing products.

  • Equity: AI is how LawnStarter plans to move faster than its size, and this role decides how that shows up for customers and Pros. Equity means you share in what that builds.
  • Base salary: $170,000 to $225,000
  • Healthcare: Medical, dental, and vision
  • Location: Fully remote (US). Evals, transcripts, and failure cases reward deep focus, and remote work protects it.
  • PTO: Flexible. We focus on results. Take what you need.

LawnStarter provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, or genetics. We comply with applicable state and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment.

jobs.title: Founding Product Manager
jobs.jd_full:
Work in New York City, NY

Work Schedule: EST │ Full overlap with US Eastern business hours (On-site)

About Pearl Talent
Pearl works with the top 1% of candidates from around the world and connects them with the best startups in the US and EU. Our clients have raised over $5B in aggregate and are backed by companies like OpenAI, a16z, and Founders Fund.

Hear why we exist, what we believe in, and who we’re building for:

About the Client
A well-funded US healthcare technology company is building the infrastructure behind healthcare payments and reimbursements, looking for a Founding Product Manager to turn its API platform into customer-facing revenue cycle management (RCM) products.

The company converts complex medical and reimbursement policies into structured, machine-readable data for healthcare organizations. It is led by a highly technical founding team and is now expanding into end-to-end RCM, co-developing new products with leading healthcare organizations.

About the Role
This is the company’s first dedicated product hire, working directly with the founders, engineers, and enterprise healthcare customers. Day to day, the role centers on discovery with RCM providers, writing PRDs, prioritizing the roadmap, and shipping API-driven products with engineering. Success means new products launched and adopted by RCM customers, a roadmap the team executes against, and a product process that can grow into a full product organization led by this hire.

Customer Discovery & Product Development

Product Strategy & Ownership

Technical Collaboration & Execution

Must-Have

Nice-to-Have

  • Prior experience as an early product hire at an early-stage or high-growth technology company

  • Familiarity with payer policies, medical coding (CPT, ICD-10), or claims workflows

jobs.jd_full:
Project Manager - People & Talent

Are you an organized, detail-oriented project manager with a passion for people, talent acquisition and performance management? Do you enjoy building efficient recruitment processes, driving projects from start to finish, enhancing the candidate and employee experience, and helping people grow and do their best work? If so, Codekeeper offers an opportunity to make a meaningful impact.

We’re looking for a proactive, hands-on and ownership-driven individual to drive recruitment, coordinate our performance management cycle, and manage people projects from inception to completion. You’ll play a key role in running goal-setting and review processes, supporting managers in giving meaningful feedback, and turning performance insights into development opportunities for our team. Along the way, you’ll refine processes, drive continuous improvement, and help us attract, develop, and retain top talent. The ideal candidate is eager to grow within the role, comfortable working cross-functionally, and ready to bring fresh ideas to strengthen our evolving HR practices.

We’re accepting applications over the next two months and will close the position as soon as we find the right fit, so we encourage early applications.

Role Description

The Project Manager - People & Talent will be responsible for managing HR projects, systems, and procedures across Codekeeper. They will oversee recruitment activities, including sourcing, attracting, screening, interviewing, and assessing potential candidates, and onboarding new employees. They will also coordinate the performance management cycle, including goal-setting, performance reviews, and feedback processes, and work with managers to support employee development, recognize strong performance, and address performance concerns constructively. Each of these areas is run as a project: you’ll plan the work, set deadlines, keep stakeholders aligned, and see it through to completion.

Key Responsibilities

Recruiting

  • Source, post, and optimize job openings on various platforms
  • Design and manage application and screening processes according to company policies
  • Expand recruitment reach and improve candidate engagement

Screening & Interviewing

  • Collaborate with department managers to define role requirements
  • Conduct initial screening calls and evaluate candidates based on established criteria

Offer Management

  • Present job offers to successful candidates, detailing position terms, remuneration, and benefits

Performance Management

  • Coordinate performance management processes, including goal-setting, reviews, and feedback
  • Support managers and employees throughout the performance cycle
  • Help identify development needs and support employee growth

Project Management ​​​​​

  • Plan and lead people projects from inception to completion, setting realistic deadlines and monitoring progress
  • Act as the bridge between HR, team leads, and department heads, ensuring a clear flow of information
  • Identify obstacles early and find practical solutions to keep projects moving
  • Contribute to cross-functional projects across the company

Process Optimization​

  • Explore new platforms, tools, and strategies to enhance recruitment and performance processes
  • Document procedures and workflows in the relevant HR folders

HR Management

  • Develop, structure, and document HR procedures aligned with company policies
  • Manage onboarding processes to ensure a seamless transition for new hires

Employee Relations

  • Organize three online team gatherings and one offline team event per year to foster engagement and a strong company culture

About the Company

Codekeeper was founded by tech industry professionals to revolutionize software escrow for the cloud era. We offer state-of-the-art software escrow solutions that mitigate third-party risks in business operations. As a remote-first company with a central office in The Hague, we prioritize a healthy, resilient organization to support the development of our robust app.

What We Offer

  • Passionate and fun-loving colleagues
  • Startup mindset with ample opportunities for growth
  • Regular team activities and gatherings
  • Comprehensive onboarding process with a dedicated ramp-up period
  • A supportive team that values open communication and direct feedback
  • A chance to excel in your career and make a difference

Skills We Are Looking For

  • Proficiency in English, both written and verbal
  • Ability to adapt and multitask in a fast-paced environment
  • Strong organizational, analytical, and strategic thinking skills
  • Proficiency in contemporary web tools such as Zapier, Linear, and Google Docs

Required Experience

  • Professional Experience: A minimum of 1–2 years in a similar HR, recruitment, or people-focused project role
  • Background in recruitment, with experience in screening, interviewing, and assessing candidates
  • Experience in performance coaching, training and development
  • Experience managing projects or leading process improvements, in HR or another field

Additional Info

  • Job Location: Remote
  • Join us to shape the future of software escrow!

How To Apply

To apply, use the Apply button on this listing. In your application, tell us how you would like to fill this position. There are no right answers or expectations. Show us your role in our company’s future and our role in yours, address some of the work we do, and introduce yourself as a colleague.

Please note: Applications and follow-ups sent through any other channel, such as our customer website chat, support email or direct messages to team members, won’t be considered. Need an accessibility adjustment to apply? Visit Our Careers Page for how to reach us.
